questions.question: A due-date column suddenly shows numbers like 46143 instead of dates. What is the right fix?

answerOptions.rationale: The data is fine; retyping wastes time and risks typos.

answerOptions.text: Add 1900 to each number with a formula
answerOptions.rationale: Serial numbers count days from 1-Jan-1900; adding 1900 gives wrong dates.

answerOptions.text: Change the cells to a date format; the values are already correct
answerOptions.rationale: Excel stores dates as serial numbers, so only the format needs changing.

answerOptions.text: Wrap each cell in TEXT to turn it into a date
answerOptions.rationale: TEXT returns text, not a real date you can calculate with.

questions.question: A factory works Monday to Saturday with only Sunday off. Which formula counts its working days between B2 and C2, skipping the named range Holidays?

answerOptions.rationale: Plain NETWORKDAYS always treats Saturday and Sunday as weekends.

questions.question: =DATEDIF($K$1,B2,"Y") returns #NUM!, where K1 is the as-on date and B2 is the date of birth. Why?

answerOptions.text: The start date must come before the end date
answerOptions.rationale: DATEDIF needs the earlier date first; here the dates are swapped.
